# Overview
Our lab today focuses on section **3. Simulation studies** of the paper by
[Li and Lin (2025)](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-applied-statistics/volume-19/issue-3/Integrative-ecological-regression-analysis-of-US-county-and-state-level/10.1214/25-AOAS2055.full),
which you have read in advance.
Specifically, we'll discuss the goals of the simulation study, the choices the
authors made in designing their data generating mechanisms, how those choices
may affect the results of the study, and interpretation of those results as
presented in Tables 2 and 3.
# Schedule
1. First, to get us all refreshed on the context, I'll give a **brief overview**
   of their method.
2. Please form groups of 2-3 students. **Open a shared Google Doc**, giving
   access to everyone in your group.
3. List what were the main goals of the simulation study performed by the
   authors and what metrics they considered in assessing their method.
   - How do Emp SE and Est SE in Tables 2 and 3 differ? How large a discrepancy
     would concern you, and what additional information would you need to
     judge it? Would the average estimated SE reveal how much the estimated
     SEs vary across datasets?
   - How many simulation replications were used? If true coverage were 95%,
     how much Monte Carlo variability would you expect in the reported
     coverage? Use this to assess a reported value. Do the authors quantify
     this simulation uncertainty?
4. Discuss how the authors generate their **simulated datasets**, as described
   in Section 3.1 of the paper. In your Google Doc, have one group member write
   down **pseudo-code** to generate a single dataset. Identify what is
   generated once and what is regenerated in each replication, and state any
   details you need to infer.
   - Which quantities are independent, and conditional on what? How does your
     simulation preserve dependence among individual outcomes and between
     county totals and state demographic counts?
   - The simulations use independent normal county random effects. If you
     instead wanted correlated county effects with a specified positive-definite
     covariance matrix, how would you generate them efficiently using the
     Cholesky decomposition described in [Unit 9](/units/unit9-sim.html)?
5. Next, **discuss the specific choices** the authors made in designing their
   simulated datasets. As you discuss, **write down those choices** in your
   Google Doc.
6. As a group, pick the **two most important choices** and justify why you
   picked them in the Google Doc.
7. With those choices in mind, brainstorm and write how you might simulate the
   data differently. Describe a data generating process that would challenge
   an assumption or approximation of the fitted model, and predict how it
   might affect coverage or standard error estimates.
8. Finally, have one group member export the Google Doc to PDF and submit it
   **as a group** for the "Lab 6" assignment on **Pensive**. Only one
   submission is needed per group.
9. Time allowing, after your group submits its assignment to Pensive, find
   another group that has also completed its submission and discuss your
   answers.
